The apavāda (annulling exception) of ekārgala and the other doṣas
The doṣas of ekārgala, upagraha, pāta, lattā, yāmitra, kartarī and udayāsta perish when the lagna is endowed with the strength of the Moon and the Sun — just as the doṣās (nights) perish at sunrise. (68)

[ṭīkā] Ekārgala (khārjūra), and upagraha, pāta, lattā, yāmitrī, kartarī, udayāsta (to be described below) — these doṣas are destroyed in the marriage lagna when the Sun and the Moon are strong; just as the darkness of night is destroyed when the Sun rises. (68)

The upagraha-nakṣatra [is to be shunned] in Kuru and Bāhlīka; the pāta-struck nakṣatra in [?] and Vaṅga; the lattā-struck nakṣatra in Saurāṣṭra and Śālva; but the vedha-struck one is indeed to be shunned in every country. (69)

[ṭīkā] In Kuru-deśa and Bāhlīka-deśa (which lies in the west) the upagraha-nakṣatra is to be rejected, not in other countries. In Vaṅga (in the east) and in Magadha and the rest the pāta doṣa (Caṇḍīśa, Caṇḍāyudha) is to be rejected. In Saurāṣṭra and Śālva (in the west) lattā is to be rejected; and vedha is to be rejected everywhere. In some [works] yuti-doṣa is assigned to Gauḍa, and yāmitrī to the Yāmuna country. (69)

When the nakṣatra-numbers of Moon and Sun are added [and divided], if the remainder is 0, 1, 4, 6, 10, 11, 15, 18, 19 or 20, these bear the name of the ten yogas (daśa-yoga). (70)

[ṭīkā] Add together the nakṣatra numbers of the Sun and the Moon and divide by 27; if the remainder is any of 0, 1, 4, 6, 10, 11, 15, 18, 19, 20, the designation daśa-yoga applies. (70)

The result of the ten doṣa-yogas, and their apavāda (exception)
Wind, fire, [injury from] the king, thieves, death, disease, quarrel and loss [result] when the yoga-number, being halved, is even … [the middle of the verse — the reckoning of the "lines" (rekhā) — is not recoverable from the scan and is left untranslated] … but in this, when there is a great Moon-yoga, it becomes a giver of good, the two standing on a single line. (71)

[ṭīkā] … half … add 5 (manu) … thus: an odd number 15, adding one makes 16, half of that is 8 … [the ṭīkā breaks off and continues on the following page]

The means of parihāra (remedy) for planetary derangement

A bath prepared with water containing lājā (parched grain), kuṣṭha, balā, priyaṅgu, mustā, siddhārtha (white mustard), niśā (turmeric) and dāru (devadāru), together with [śara-]puṅkhā and lodhra, is declared to destroy the evil arising from the grahas. A cow, a conch, a red bull, gold, a yellow garment, a white horse, a black cow, a buffalo and a goat [?] — these are the dakṣiṇās, reckoned from the Sun onward. ‖ 16 ‖

[ṭīkā] For the sake of the parihāra of afflicted grahas, the bathing herbs are: (lājā) parched grain, or else lajjāvatī; kūṭha; (balā) bhīmalī; mālakāṅganī; mustā; sarṣapa (mustard); devadāra; haridrā (turmeric); śarapuṅkhā; lodha. Bathing with all of these mixed into the water removes the ariṣṭa (evil) of the grahas. As to the dakṣiṇā (sacerdotal fee), it is said: to propitiate the Sun, a cow; the Moon, a conch; Mars, a red bull; Mercury, gold; Jupiter, a yellow garment; Venus, a horse; [Saturn,] a black cow; Rāhu, a khaḍga [?]; and to Ketu a goat is to be given as dakṣiṇā. ‖ 16 ‖ (Śā°)

[ṭīkā, continuing v.71] … if [the Moon] is strong and placed in a kendra, then the doṣa of the ten doṣas does not obtain — this is the opinion of another work. (71) (metre: Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

Bāṇa-doṣa, called pañcaka (the five "arrows")
The elapsed tithis increased by the lagna and divided [by nine]: when the remainder is of the number 8, 2, 4, 6 or 1 [respectively] — disease, fire, the king, the thief, and death [are the bāṇas]. This bāṇa is well known among the southerners. (72)

[ṭīkā] Add to the lagna the tithis elapsed from the śukla-pakṣa pratipad and divide by 9. If the remainder is 8 it is roga-bāṇa (disease-arrow); with remainder 2, agni (fire); with 4, rāja (king); with 6, cora (thief); with 1, mṛtyu (death). This is current in the Dākṣiṇātya (Maharashtra) countries, not elsewhere. (72) (metre: Śālinī)

The bāṇa according to the eastern opinion, with its apavāda (exception)
[Adding severally] 6, 3, 1, 8 and 4 to the degrees elapsed of the Sun since the saṅkrānti … when, on division, the remainder is five [in a given case], the bāṇa is named disease, fire, king, thief and death [respectively]; and when, on dividing by nine, five remains from the sum of the [nine] remainders, it is sa-śalya ("with the barb"). (73)

[ṭīkā] To the nirayaṇa degrees elapsed of the Sun from the saṅkrānti add separately 6, 3, 1, 8 and 4, divide each by 9, and know the bāṇa from whichever number leaves a remainder of 5. If 5 remains in the case of 6, it is roga-bāṇa; so with 3, agni; with 1, rāja; with 8, cora; with 4, mṛtyu — this is the kāṣṭha-śalya (wooden-barbed) bāṇa. Then, in the manner stated above, add the Sun's elapsed degrees to the numbers 6 and the rest, take the remainders after dividing by 9, add all nine remainders together and divide by 9: if 5 remains, know it to be sa-śalya, i.e. attended by an iron barb; with any other remainder it is free of the barb. The sa-śalya is exceedingly to be condemned. (73) (metre: Mālinī)

Its parihāra (neutralisation), threefold, by difference of time
[The mūla of v.74 is heavily damaged; only the correspondences confirmed by the ṭīkā can be given:] the thief- and disease-bāṇas [are to be shunned] by day/night as stated, the king-bāṇa by day, the fire-bāṇa always, [the death-bāṇa] at the two twilights; and by weekday — on Saturn's day the king-, on Mercury's the death-, on Mars's the fire- and thief-[bāṇa] …; and by undertaking — in the vrata-bandha, house-protection, royal service, journey and marriage respectively. (74)

[ṭīkā] The thief- and disease-bāṇas are to be shunned at night, the king-bāṇa by day, the fire-bāṇa always, that is both by day and by night, and the death-bāṇa at the time of sandhyā (twilight). Further, on Saturday the king-, on Wednesday the death-, on Tuesday the fire- and thief-[bāṇa are shunned], on Sunday … [the ṭīkā continues on the next chunk]

[ṭīkā] The sense of these four verses [20–23] emerges from the diagram. For the month of Pauṣa write the twelve tithi (lunar days) in order beginning from pratipadā; for Māgha begin from dvitīyā; likewise Phālguna from the 3rd, Caitra from the 4th, Vaiśākha from the 5th, Jyeṣṭha from the 6th, Āṣāḍha from the 7th, Śrāvaṇa from the 8th, Bhādrapada from the 9th, Āśvina from the 10th, Kārttika from the 11th and Mārgaśīrṣa from the 12th. Know trayodaśī as equivalent to tṛtīyā, caturdaśī to caturthī, and pañcadaśī to pañcamī. The results are written in the diagram in the order east and so on; take them exactly so. || 20–23 || (Śā.)

The sum of tithi, ṛkṣa (= nakṣatra, lunar mansion) and vāra (weekday), divided in three separate places by the mountains (7), the elephants (8) and fire (3), — if in the first place [the remainder is] nought, [the traveller becomes] utterly wretched[?]; in the middle, loss of wealth; and in the last, death results. If in [all] three places a figure is left over, comfort and victory are declared. || 24 ||

[ṭīkā] Tithi here is taken from the beginning of the śukla-pakṣa. Add the tithi, the nakṣatra and the vāra, and set the sum down in three places; divide the one by 7, the second by 8, [and the third by 3][?]. If the first leaves zero, the traveller will be wretched; if the second leaves zero, loss of wealth; if the third leaves zero, death. If all three places leave a figure, then comfort and victory. || 24 || (Vasantatilakā)

THE ĀḌALA AND BHRAMAṆA DOṢA (afflictions)

The measure from the Sun's constellation to the Moon's constellation, left with the mountains (7) as remainder, [?] — the Mahāḍala is not commended; from a remainder of three or six it [the other, Bhramaṇa] arises. || 25 ||

[ṭīkā] Count from the Sun's nakṣatra up to the Moon's nakṣatra; divide that figure by 7. If 7 remains, the doṣa named Mahāḍala occurs — this is not good. If 3 or 6 remain, the inauspicious doṣa named Bhramaṇa occurs. One should not travel in these; and in the Āḍa doṣa every auspicious undertaking is forbidden. || 25 || (Pramāṇikā)

THE YOGA NAMED HIMBARA

The Moon's constellation is to be reckoned from the Sun's constellation; joined with the tithi counted from the beginning of the pakṣa and with the weekday, [the sum] divided by nine — if the remainder is the mountains (7), that is Himbara, and it is most excellent for setting out. || 26 ||

[ṭīkā] Whatever the count from the Sun's nakṣatra up to the Moon's nakṣatra, add to it the current tithi reckoned from pratipadā, together with the vāra and the nakṣatra, and divide by 9. If 7 remains, the yoga named Himbara occurs; this is most auspicious. These merits and defects are well known among the southerners. || 26 || (U. Jā.)

The apavāda (annulling exception) of ekārgala and the other doṣas
The doṣas of ekārgala, upagraha, pāta, lattā, yāmitra, kartarī and udayāsta perish when the lagna is endowed with the strength of the Moon and the Sun — just as the doṣās (nights) perish at sunrise. (68)

[ṭīkā] Ekārgala (khārjūra), and upagraha, pāta, lattā, yāmitrī, kartarī, udayāsta (to be described below) — these doṣas are destroyed in the marriage lagna when the Sun and the Moon are strong; just as the darkness of night is destroyed when the Sun rises. (68)

The upagraha-nakṣatra [is to be shunned] in Kuru and Bāhlīka; the pāta-struck nakṣatra in [?] and Vaṅga; the lattā-struck nakṣatra in Saurāṣṭra and Śālva; but the vedha-struck one is indeed to be shunned in every country. (69)

[ṭīkā] In Kuru-deśa and Bāhlīka-deśa (which lies in the west) the upagraha-nakṣatra is to be rejected, not in other countries. In Vaṅga (in the east) and in Magadha and the rest the pāta doṣa (Caṇḍīśa, Caṇḍāyudha) is to be rejected. In Saurāṣṭra and Śālva (in the west) lattā is to be rejected; and vedha is to be rejected everywhere. In some [works] yuti-doṣa is assigned to Gauḍa, and yāmitrī to the Yāmuna country. (69)

When the nakṣatra-numbers of Moon and Sun are added [and divided], if the remainder is 0, 1, 4, 6, 10, 11, 15, 18, 19 or 20, these bear the name of the ten yogas (daśa-yoga). (70)

[ṭīkā] Add together the nakṣatra numbers of the Sun and the Moon and divide by 27; if the remainder is any of 0, 1, 4, 6, 10, 11, 15, 18, 19, 20, the designation daśa-yoga applies. (70)

The result of the ten doṣa-yogas, and their apavāda (exception)
Wind, fire, [injury from] the king, thieves, death, disease, quarrel and loss [result] when the yoga-number, being halved, is even … [the middle of the verse — the reckoning of the "lines" (rekhā) — is not recoverable from the scan and is left untranslated] … but in this, when there is a great Moon-yoga, it becomes a giver of good, the two standing on a single line. (71)

[ṭīkā] … half … add 5 (manu) … thus: an odd number 15, adding one makes 16, half of that is 8 … [the ṭīkā breaks off and continues on the following page]

[ṭīkā, continuing v.71] … if [the Moon] is strong and placed in a kendra, then the doṣa of the ten doṣas does not obtain — this is the opinion of another work. (71) (metre: Śārdūlavikrīḍita)

Bāṇa-doṣa, called pañcaka (the five "arrows")
The elapsed tithis increased by the lagna and divided [by nine]: when the remainder is of the number 8, 2, 4, 6 or 1 [respectively] — disease, fire, the king, the thief, and death [are the bāṇas]. This bāṇa is well known among the southerners. (72)

[ṭīkā] Add to the lagna the tithis elapsed from the śukla-pakṣa pratipad and divide by 9. If the remainder is 8 it is roga-bāṇa (disease-arrow); with remainder 2, agni (fire); with 4, rāja (king); with 6, cora (thief); with 1, mṛtyu (death). This is current in the Dākṣiṇātya (Maharashtra) countries, not elsewhere. (72) (metre: Śālinī)

The bāṇa according to the eastern opinion, with its apavāda (exception)
[Adding severally] 6, 3, 1, 8 and 4 to the degrees elapsed of the Sun since the saṅkrānti … when, on division, the remainder is five [in a given case], the bāṇa is named disease, fire, king, thief and death [respectively]; and when, on dividing by nine, five remains from the sum of the [nine] remainders, it is sa-śalya ("with the barb"). (73)

[ṭīkā] The sense of these four verses [20–23] emerges from the diagram. For the month of Pauṣa write the twelve tithi (lunar days) in order beginning from pratipadā; for Māgha begin from dvitīyā; likewise Phālguna from the 3rd, Caitra from the 4th, Vaiśākha from the 5th, Jyeṣṭha from the 6th, Āṣāḍha from the 7th, Śrāvaṇa from the 8th, Bhādrapada from the 9th, Āśvina from the 10th, Kārttika from the 11th and Mārgaśīrṣa from the 12th. Know trayodaśī as equivalent to tṛtīyā, caturdaśī to caturthī, and pañcadaśī to pañcamī. The results are written in the diagram in the order east and so on; take them exactly so. || 20–23 || (Śā.)

The sum of tithi, ṛkṣa (= nakṣatra, lunar mansion) and vāra (weekday), divided in three separate places by the mountains (7), the elephants (8) and fire (3), — if in the first place [the remainder is] nought, [the traveller becomes] utterly wretched[?]; in the middle, loss of wealth; and in the last, death results. If in [all] three places a figure is left over, comfort and victory are declared. || 24 ||

[ṭīkā] Tithi here is taken from the beginning of the śukla-pakṣa. Add the tithi, the nakṣatra and the vāra, and set the sum down in three places; divide the one by 7, the second by 8, [and the third by 3][?]. If the first leaves zero, the traveller will be wretched; if the second leaves zero, loss of wealth; if the third leaves zero, death. If all three places leave a figure, then comfort and victory. || 24 || (Vasantatilakā)

THE ĀḌALA AND BHRAMAṆA DOṢA (afflictions)

The measure from the Sun's constellation to the Moon's constellation, left with the mountains (7) as remainder, [?] — the Mahāḍala is not commended; from a remainder of three or six it [the other, Bhramaṇa] arises. || 25 ||

[ṭīkā] Count from the Sun's nakṣatra up to the Moon's nakṣatra; divide that figure by 7. If 7 remains, the doṣa named Mahāḍala occurs — this is not good. If 3 or 6 remain, the inauspicious doṣa named Bhramaṇa occurs. One should not travel in these; and in the Āḍa doṣa every auspicious undertaking is forbidden. || 25 || (Pramāṇikā)

THE YOGA NAMED HIMBARA

The Moon's constellation is to be reckoned from the Sun's constellation; joined with the tithi counted from the beginning of the pakṣa and with the weekday, [the sum] divided by nine — if the remainder is the mountains (7), that is Himbara, and it is most excellent for setting out. || 26 ||

[ṭīkā] Whatever the count from the Sun's nakṣatra up to the Moon's nakṣatra, add to it the current tithi reckoned from pratipadā, together with the vāra and the nakṣatra, and divide by 9. If 7 remains, the yoga named Himbara occurs; this is most auspicious. These merits and defects are well known among the southerners. || 26 || (U. Jā.)
